Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `main` at `66707437b53aa54446d661c8f409795577d13ead`. The `/answer` was auto-posted because no clarification was needed; there are no Q-ID answers to resolve. No integration branch was specified.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion  
Reuse-audit: extends `review_autofix.yml`’s existing PR gate, checkout, and stale-base guard  
Scope-mode justification: Changing only the checkout expression would correct many dispatched reviews but leave fork-head and head-movement cases unsafe. The plan includes those guards and a check for executable project configuration before an agent starts. This follows `unattended_system_instructions.md` §6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed. No new subsystem is needed.

## Automation and delivery
- **Existing code only:** extend `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`; add no standalone script, supervisor, or database operation.
- **Entry point:** the existing `review_autofix.yml` review job, invoked by PR events and by `workflow_dispatch` through the sweep and other dispatchers. No new trigger or operator step.
- **Budget:** target completion within 60 minutes.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` — gate output, checkout selection, pre-agent safety check, and head-consistency guard.
- `tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py` — extend its existing executable gate fixture for dispatch and fork cases.
- `tests/test_review_autofix_merge_precheck.py` and/or `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py` — update the old checkout-expression assertion and cover checkout, file-read, and stale-head contracts.
- `agents.md` — record the checkout and trust-boundary behavior if it changes.
- `changelog.d/5824-dispatched-review-pr-head.md` — user-visible fix; do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Functions and data structures
1. Extend the gate’s existing `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}` result with `.head.repo.full_name`; use its existing `.head.sha`. Add a `review_checkout_sha` gate output only for a valid, same-repository PR head. Do not add an API request. GitHub documents this GET endpoint and its repository-read permission. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?utm_source=openai))
2. Make **Checkout repo** select the event PR-head SHA, otherwise `needs.gate.outputs.review_checkout_sha`, and use `github.sha` only for the existing no-PR push route. A dispatched PR with a missing, malformed, or cross-repository head must skip review rather than read default-branch files against a PR diff.
3. Before any agent launch, reject a PR-head checkout containing project-supplied OpenCode configuration or plugins unless a verified isolation mechanism prevents their loading. Do not treat an explicit `OPENCODE_CONFIG` file as isolation: OpenCode also discovers project configuration and automatically loads project plugins. Keep executable support staged from the verified workflow commit. ([dev.opencode.ai](https://dev.opencode.ai/docs/plugins/?utm_source=openai))
4. After **Checkout PR head branch**, compare the commit whose files remain in `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` with both the working checkout and the head recorded by **Collect PR metadata**. On a mismatch, use the existing `AUTOFIX_STALE_BASE_SKIP` path before reviewers, editor, resolver, hand-off, or merge authorization. Do not silently review the older file tree.

**API/interface changes:** Add the internal gate output `review_checkout_sha`; preserve existing outputs, workflow inputs, and public interfaces. The representative pattern is the gate’s existing PR fetch and `head_sha` output, followed by the existing stale-base soft-exit.

**Data flow:** PR gate reads one authenticated PR payload → validates head repository and SHA → checkout materializes that SHA in `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` → workspace initialization and metadata collection run → head-consistency check authorizes agent file reads. The trusted support checkout remains separately pinned.

## Decisions
### D1 — Materialize the reviewed head in the source workspace
- **Chosen:** Checkout the gate-verified, same-repository PR SHA into `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` on dispatched runs.
- **Alternatives considered:** Repoint each reviewer, editor, resolver, context builder, and Semble reader to `WORKSPACE_PATH`.
- **Why:** One checkout corrects their shared file source without competing path-selection rules.

### D2 — Refuse unsupported or inconsistent review inputs
- **Chosen:** Skip dispatched fork/unknown-head reviews and stale file-tree reviews; fail closed on executable project configuration before agent launch.
- **Alternatives considered:** Fall back to `github.sha`, accept a moved branch, or rely solely on OpenCode environment flags.
- **Why:** None proves that the files an agent reads are the authorized PR head. A reported OpenCode project-plugin loading bypass also makes flags alone an insufficient security assumption; verify behavior on the pinned toolchain rather than relying on that report as proof for this repository’s version. ([github.com](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/49836?utm_source=openai))

## Security considerations
The PR head is untrusted; the review job has credentials and model access. Validate the PR number, full-name match, and 40-hex head SHA from the authenticated gate response before selecting a dispatched checkout. Do not interpolate a branch name into workflow script source, execute PR-head helpers, or substitute a default-branch checkout when validation fails. The pre-agent check must cover project plugin and configuration paths that OpenCode could load; keep the trusted support checkout and `SCRIPT_REF` selection unchanged. Test a PR that adds a plugin alongside an ordinary added file, including the path where checkout succeeds but the agent must not start. No new endpoint or authorization surface is introduced. Checkout v5 persists credentials by default, which makes preventing untrusted code execution in this workspace consequential. ([github.com](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/main/README.md))

## Risks and edge cases
- A push between gate evaluation, metadata collection, and branch fetch can produce three different heads. Compare the actual file tree, not just two Git references.
- A fork, deleted head repository, failed PR read, or unavailable SHA must not yield a default-branch “review.”
- Preserve `pull_request` behavior and the no-PR `claude/**` push route; do not change trusted support-ref checkout.
- **Codebase conflict:** issue line references describe an earlier revision. On this planning ref, **Checkout repo** is around line 2481 and `reviewer_opencode_workspace` around line 4501. `tests/test_review_autofix_merge_precheck.py` currently asserts the expression that needs updating.
- The October 1 Claude progress comment describes work on a separate project branch. It is context, not evidence that its changes exist on this planning ref.

## Testing and verification
- Extend the existing gate fixture for same-repo dispatch, `pull_request`, fork dispatch, missing/malformed head, and no-PR push; assert that no invalid case can authorize a review or merge.
- Assert the checkout expression resolves to the PR-head SHA for dispatch and that the reviewer workspace contains a file added only by that head. Cover the workspace/metadata/branch-fetch movement cases and ensure they skip agent steps.
- Test the project-configuration safety check before agent launch. Run the focused review workflow tests, workflow-size guard, YAML/actionlint checks, and relevant CI checks on the repository’s pinned tooling. Measure `review_autofix.yml` after editing; it is currently 458,436 bytes, below the 480,000-byte split guard.

## Pre-execution self-check
The plan names the existing entry point, reuse path, trust boundary, affected files, tests, and fail-closed behavior. No private scalar or missing clarification answer is required. No repository files were modified during planning.
